architecture.title: Architecture & Documentation Center
architecture.subtitle: Explore SkyForge's six-layer engine architecture, 12-stage pipeline, and complete documentation

orchestration.title: Orchestration Layer
orchestration.responsibility: Chains layer responsibilities together, schedules the full pipeline, and generates a trusted evidence package.

agentStrategy.title: Agent Strategy Layer
agentStrategy.responsibility: Multiple agents handle requirement parsing, LLR / contract / code generation, repair, and MISRA adaptation.

verifierChain.title: Verifier Toolchain Layer
verifierChain.responsibility: A pluggable chain of formal and static analysis tools: Z3 / CBMC / Cppcheck / GCC.

simulation.title: Simulation & Verification Layer (SIL/PIL/HIL)
simulation.responsibility: Covers pure software simulation (SIL), QEMU processor simulation (PIL), and real hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), with fault injection and ARINC 653 partition scheduling.

llmClient.title: LLM Client Layer
llmClient.responsibility: A unified LLM interface: Mock / cloud API / local OpenAI-compatible clients and routing.

protocols.title: Infrastructure Protocol Layer
protocols.responsibility: Protocols / abstract base classes / mode guards and execution contracts that define the interaction surface for upper layers.

pipeline.title: 12-Stage Pipeline
pipeline.description: The complete pipeline from requirement reception to evidence package generation, powered by the six-layer architecture

quickstart.title: Step-by-Step Guide
quickstart.description: Follow these 5 steps to get up and running with the SkyForge workflow

source.title: Choose a runtime source
source.description: Pick the execution mode that fits your needs: cloud (cloud models) or local (local models).

model.title: Configure model connection
model.description: Configure the cloud API endpoint and key, or a local Ollama/LM Studio endpoint, to make the LLM service available.

firstTask.title: Create your first code generation task
firstTask.description: Enter natural-language requirements on the code generation page, choose a programming language, and launch a full pipeline task.

results.title: Review run results

evidence.title: Understand verification evidence

item1.q: Which programming languages does SkyForge support?
item1.a: It currently supports code generation and verification for C (MISRA-C:2012), C++ (MISRA C++ / JSF AV C++), and Python (defense safety standards).

item2.q: What are the two execution mode profiles?
item2.a: cloud mode connects to a cloud LLM service for real inference; local mode uses a locally deployed Ollama/LM Studio so data never leaves your intranet. mock mode is only used for development and debugging when there is no backend.

item3.a: Yes. SkyForge ships 57 built-in MISRA-C auto-fix rules. Violations found by Cppcheck scans are automatically repaired by the code_repairer agent and re-verified.

item4.q: Which tools are used for formal verification?
item4.a: The Z3 SMT solver performs contract verification and CBMC performs bounded model checking. Together they form the pluggable VerifierChain.

item5.q: How does HITL human review work?
item5.a: At the three key checkpoints — requirements, contracts, and code — the system decides whether human approval is needed based on a risk assessment. HITL can be enabled or disabled in system settings.

misraC.name: MISRA-C
misraC.description: MISRA C is the C language coding standard published by the Motor Industry Software Reliability Association (MISRA), aimed at improving the safety and reliability of embedded systems. SkyForge implements 10 red-line rules and 56 fixers.

environment.name: Environment & Compilation
environment.r1: Rule 1.1: Do not use undefined, unspecified, or implementation-defined behavior
environment.r2: Rule 1.2: No code that violates standard C
environment.r3: Rule 2.1: A project shall not contain unreachable code

typeSafety.name: Type Safety
typeSafety.r1: Rule 8.13: Pointer parameters shall be declared as pointers to const
typeSafety.r2: Rule 10.1: Operands of operators shall not have inappropriate essential types
typeSafety.r3: Rule 11.1: Conversions shall not be performed between pointer and integer types

memory.name: Memory & Resources
memory.r1: Rule 17.6: Dynamic memory allocation from the malloc family shall not be used
memory.r2: Rule 21.3: Standard library memory management functions shall not be used

controlFlow.name: Control Flow
controlFlow.r1: Rule 14.4: An else branch must follow if/else if/else chains
controlFlow.r2: Rule 15.1: The goto statement shall not be used
controlFlow.r3: Rule 16.3: A switch statement must have a default branch

misraCpp.name: MISRA C++ / JSF AV C++
misraCpp.description: MISRA C++ is the safety coding standard for C++, while JSF AV C++ is the C++ coding standard of the Joint Strike Fighter project. SkyForge implements 5 JSF AV C++ red-line rules.

typeSafety.name: Type Safety
typeSafety.r1: AV Rule 4: All variables must be initialized at declaration
typeSafety.r2: AV Rule 8: Do not use raw arrays; use std::array or std::vector

memory.name: Memory Management
memory.r1: AV Rule 15: Manage resources with RAII
memory.r2: AV Rule 16: Do not use bare new/delete; use smart pointers

exceptions.name: Exception Safety
exceptions.r1: AV Rule 39: Destructors must not throw exceptions
exceptions.r2: AV Rule 42: Provide the strong exception safety guarantee

pythonSafety.name: Python Defense Safety Standard
pythonSafety.description: A Python safety coding standard for defense and aerospace, ensuring the reliability of Python code in safety-critical environments. SkyForge implements 3 red-line rules and 4 fixers.

typeSafety.name: Type Safety
typeSafety.r1: Rule 1: All functions must have type annotations
typeSafety.r2: Rule 2: Do not use eval() and exec()

security.name: Security
security.r1: Rule 3: Do not use pickle for data serialization
security.r2: Rule 4: All inputs must be validated and sanitized

reliability.name: Reliability
reliability.r1: Rule 5: Use logging instead of print output
reliability.r2: Rule 6: All resources must use context managers (with statements)

do178c.name: DO-178C Compliance Guide
do178c.description: DO-178C is the airworthiness certification standard for aviation onboard software, defining the complete software lifecycle process requirements from planning to production. SkyForge provides engineering supporting evidence and does not replace airworthiness certification.

objectives.name: Core Objectives (19 Assessable Objectives)
objectives.r1: OBJ-1 ~ OBJ-5: Requirements process (problem reports, traceability, HLR/LLR)
objectives.r2: OBJ-6 ~ OBJ-9: Design and coding (architecture, source code, low-level requirements)
objectives.r3: OBJ-10 ~ OBJ-14: Verification process (independence, coverage analysis)
objectives.r4: OBJ-15 ~ OBJ-19: Configuration and quality (configuration management, quality assurance, tool qualification)

dalLevels.name: DAL Coverage Requirements
dalLevels.r1: DAL A (Catastrophic): MC/DC coverage + all 19 objectives
